evidence.claim: Atkinson Academy's 1803 building replaced a schoolhouse destroyed by fire the year before.
evidence.quote: The original building, constructed in 1789, was destroyed by fire on November 15, 1802, and the present building was completed in 1803.

evidence.claim: The institution itself began in 1787 as a boys' school, founded by Stephen Peabody, Nathaniel Peabody and William Cogswell, and admitted girls from 1791.
evidence.quote: Atkinson Academy was founded in 1787 as an all-boys school by the Reverend Stephen Peabody, General Nathaniel Peabody, and Dr. William Cogswell. It began admitting girls in 1791.

evidence.claim: The surviving building is a work of master builder Ebenezer Clifford.
evidence.quote: It is a rare surviving work of Ebenezer Clifford, a prominent master builder of the southern New Hampshire during that period.

evidence.claim: Its clapboarded, two-story front carries a tower with an open octagonal belfry and cupola.
evidence.quote: The original main building is a large two-story wood-frame building, with a hip roof and clapboarded exterior.  A tower with open octagonal belfry and cupola rises at the center of the roof.

evidence.claim: Modern wings extend behind it, giving the school a rough W shape.
evidence.quote: Modern wings extend to the rear of this building, giving the building a rough W shape.

evidence.claim: Pilasters and a pedimented gable set apart the three central bays of its seven-bay facade.
evidence.quote: The main facade is seven bays wide, with the central three set apart by pilasters and a pedimented gable.

evidence.claim: Names on Chester's gravestones can identify the maker as well as the person buried.
evidence.quote: particularly unusual for the large number of grave markers that were signed by their carvers.

evidence.quote: This has enabled researchers to differentiate their styles from each other, making possible the identification of their work in other regional cemeteries.

evidence.quote: The cemetery was established in 1751, and became the town's main burying ground.
